title: Divergence, curl, and differential identities
terms: divergence; curl; solenoidal field; irrotational field; Laplacian; vector Laplacian.

exposition.text:
For F = (P, Q, R), divergence is ∇ · F = P + Q + R , a scalar measuring local outward flux.
x y z
Curl is ∇ × F = (R − Q , P − R , Q − P ), measuring local circulation. A divergence-free field
y z z x x y
is solenoidal; a curl-free field is irrotational. The Laplacian of f is ∆f = ∇ · ∇f.
When second derivatives are continuous, ∇ × ∇f = 0 and ∇ · (∇ × F) = 0. These are neces-
sary tests for potential representations. A curl-free field on an open simply connected region is
conservative, but holes can obstruct a global potential. Divergence-free alone does not imply
curl-free or conservativity.
For a vector field, the vector Laplacian applies the scalar Laplacian to each component. With
continuous second partial derivatives, ∇ × (∇ × F) = ∇(∇ · F) − ∆F. The product rule is
∇ × (ϕF) = ∇ϕ × F + ϕ(∇ × F).

question.text:
2
For F = (axy, y + bz, xz), which pair (a, b) makes ∇ · F identically equal to x?
(A) (0, 0) (B) (2, 0) (C) (−2, 0) only (D) a = −2 with any real b (E) No pair

solution.text:
The divergence is ay+2y+x = (a+2)y+x, independent of b. Thus a = −2 and b is arbitrary;
a condition on curl was not requested.

question.text:

For every twice continuously differentiable vector field F on an open subset of R , which iden-
tity holds, with the Laplacian applied componentwise?
(A) ∇ × (∇ × F) = ∇(∇ · F) − ∆F (B) ∇ × (∇ × F) = ∆F
(C) ∇ × (∇ × F) = 0 (D) ∇(∇ · F) = 0
(E) ∇ × (∇ × F) = ∇(∇ · F) + ∆F

solution.text:
For F = (P, Q, R), the first component of the left side is Q + R − P − P . The first
xy xz yy zz
component of ∇(∇ · F) − ∆F is the same after the P terms cancel. The other components
xx
follow cyclically. Continuous second partials justify the interchanges.

Each component is independent of its own differentiation variable, so divergence is zero.
Moreover F = ∇(xyz), so its curl is zero; direct cross-partial differentiation gives the same
result.

question.text:
For a twice continuously differentiable scalar function f, which vector field is necessarily diver-
gence free?
(A) ∇ × (f, 0, 0)
(B) f(x, y, z), interpreted as a radial multiple (f x, f y, fz)
(C) ∇f
(D) (f, f, f)
(E) (f , 0, 0)

solution.text:
The divergence of a curl is zero because mixed partial derivatives cancel. The other fields
can have nonzero divergence; for example, ∇ · ∇f = ∆f need not vanish.
